narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found a 58% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a figure that, while not overwhelming, was sufficient to result in a denial. This decision was shaped by a combination of factors specific to your financial situation, and understanding them may help you take steps toward a successful application in the future.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about 20% had a negative checking account balance, while roughly half had no checking account at all or maintained a positive balance. A negative balance signals to the assessment that your day-to-day finances may already be under strain, which raises concerns about your ability to take on additional debt.

The second most significant factor was the length of the loan you requested — 42 months. This is more than double the average loan duration of approximately 19 months among applicants who were approved. A longer loan term means a longer period of financial commitment, and combined with your current account situation, this extended timeline amplified the concern that repayment could become difficult over time. The loan amount of 3,394 DM, while somewhat above the approved applicant average of around 2,887 DM, was a lesser concern on its own, but it compounds the picture when paired with the duration.

Interestingly, your credit history — which is categorized as "critical or other credits" — actually worked in your favor, nudging the assessment slightly toward a more positive outcome. About 35% of approved applicants share this same credit history category, so this aspect of your profile is not unusual and did provide some counterbalance to the other concerns.

Other aspects of your profile also painted a challenging picture, even if they were not among the top three drivers of the decision. Being currently unemployed is a significant concern for any lender, as it raises questions about a steady income source to meet monthly installment payments. Your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is also higher than the approved applicant average of about 2.94%, meaning the loan payments would represent a relatively larger burden on your finances. Additionally, the purpose of the loan — home repairs — is among the least common reasons for approved loans, with fewer than 2% of approved applicants borrowing for this purpose.

To improve your chances in a future application, it would be worth focusing on stabilizing your checking account balance and bringing it into positive territory before reapplying. If possible, securing employment or a verifiable income source would significantly strengthen your profile. You might also consider whether a shorter loan duration or a smaller loan amount could meet your needs, as both would reduce the perceived risk. Speaking with a financial advisor or a bank representative about your specific circumstances could help you identify the most effective path forward.
